brief: Goldman (via The Market Ear) makes the case for the "experience economy" trade heading into earnings season. Real US spending on experiences grew almost 6% YoY in Q1 2026 versus about 1% a year earlier, while broader services spending managed only around 2%, so demand is accelerating even as the consumer is under pressure elsewhere. Goldman's Consumer Experiences basket has underperformed the S&P 500 ex-AI index by roughly 14% despite that acceleration, and company prints back the demand story: Live Nation fan growth over 10%, Sphere's Wizard of Oz generating $450mn on 3.6mn tickets, Marriott luxury RevPAR up over 9%, Viking 96% booked for 2026 and 53% sold for 2027. Forward earnings for the basket keep climbing even as share prices fall from summer highs, leaving the median name near the bottom of its decade valuation range versus the equal-weighted S&P 500. The basket has recently traded negatively correlated to AI, but Goldman argues that could flip positive as more time spent with machines raises the value of physical, social experiences. Hedge funds are rebuilding exposure but remain well below prior peaks. Goldman's case rests on exposure to wealthier consumers plus improving earnings revisions and light positioning, against the risk that higher oil prices and a weakening consumer hurt travel and discretionary spend.
